skill.name: backend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Design and review production Node.js, Express, and TypeScript backends with layered architecture, Prisma repositories, Zod validation, testing, configuration, and Sentry guidance.
skill.summary: Apply consistent architecture, validation, persistence, observability, and testing patterns to Node.js backend work.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 219 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown examples, relative imports, placeholders, and TypeScript syntax. Semantic review found overbroad Sentry collection, plaintext development secrets, and direct client exposure of internal error messages.

remediation.issue: Sentry captures broad request and local-variable data with limited redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Disable local-variable capture and default request-body collection. Allowlist required fields, redact secrets recursively, and document retention and consent requirements.

remediation.issue: Development guidance stores several secrets in plaintext config.ini.
remediation.suggestion: Use a secret manager or injected environment values. Keep only non-secret settings in INI files and reject placeholder secrets during startup.

remediation.issue: The controller example sends arbitrary exception messages to clients.
remediation.suggestion: Map approved domain errors to public messages. Return a generic message for unexpected errors and retain detailed context only in protected logs.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Sentry Data Collection
semantic_findings.description: The recommended setup captures local variables, request bodies, headers, query strings, IP addresses, and user identifiers. Its scrubber removes only two headers and masks one email field.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The enabled integrations and included fields are explicit. Passwords, tokens, and personal data outside the narrow scrubber could reach Sentry.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Secret Configuration Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The guide places database, JWT, internal API, and client secrets in config.ini and gives that file highest precedence. Gitignore guidance reduces accidental commits but not plaintext exposure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The configuration examples and precedence rules are explicit. Production uses environment variables, but the recommended development file still stores secrets unencrypted.

semantic_findings.title: Internal Error Messages Returned to Clients
semantic_findings.description: The BaseController example returns error.message directly in HTTP responses. Unexpected exceptions can reveal database details, identifiers, or internal implementation information.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The response assignment is direct and lacks an allowlist of public error types. The exposure depends on which exceptions reach this handler.

content.value_statement: Backend changes often become inconsistent across routing, business logic, data access, validation, and monitoring. This skill supplies structured Node.js patterns for reliable implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Assesses backend changes with a feasibility and risk index.
Structures Express applications into routes, controllers, services, repositories, and middleware.
Applies Prisma repository, transaction, query optimization, and testing patterns.
Defines Zod schemas, validation middleware, typed DTOs, and error responses.
Adds Sentry instrumentation, async error handling, audit context, and focused tests.
limitations: Focuses on Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Zod, and Sentry.
Provides guidance and examples but does not run migrations, tests, or deployments.
Requires project-specific review for authorization, privacy, performance, and compliance.
Assumes existing abstractions such as BaseController, PrismaService, and unifiedConfig.

use_cases.title: Design a New API Feature
use_cases.description: Plan routes, validation, service logic, repository access, error handling, and tests before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Backend Architecture
use_cases.description: Identify layer violations, missing validation, direct database access, weak error boundaries, and testing gaps.

use_cases.title: Standardize a Service Team
use_cases.description: Establish shared conventions for configuration, dependency injection, monitoring, naming, repositories, and pull request review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Backend Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a [method] [path] endpoint for [goal]. Include layers, validation, errors, persistence, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Backend Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [files or diff] against these backend guidelines. List behavioral risks, architecture violations, security concerns, and missing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Transactional Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design [workflow] using Express, Prisma, and Zod. Define transaction boundaries, idempotency, error mapping, observability, and integration tests.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Legacy Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [feature] into routes, controllers, services, and repositories. Preserve behavior, add Zod validation, transaction boundaries, Sentry context, and focused tests.

output_examples.input: Plan a user creation endpoint with email validation.
output: Route delegates the request to UserController.
Controller validates input and calls UserService.
Service enforces uniqueness and invokes UserRepository.
Tests cover success, invalid email, duplicate email, and persistence failure.

output_examples.input: Review a controller that queries Prisma directly.
output: Finding: the controller bypasses service and repository boundaries.
Risk: business rules and persistence become difficult to test independently.
Recommendation: move decisions into a service and queries into a repository.

output_examples.input: Design monitoring for a payment workflow.

anti_patterns: Do not request a complete rewrite without behavioral constraints.

faq.question: Which backend stack does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Node.js services using Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Zod, and Sentry.

faq.question: Can it generate complete backend features?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation across layers, but project models, dependencies, and requirements must be provided.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. Authorization, secret handling, privacy, dependency risk, and deployment controls still require project-specific review.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide files or a diff and request findings on architecture, behavior, validation, errors, observability, and tests.

faq.question: Does it support databases beyond Prisma?
faq.answer: The architecture can transfer, but database examples and transaction guidance are written for Prisma.

faq.question: What context produces the best results?
faq.answer: Provide the feature goal, current layers, data model, API contract, error conventions, and test commands.
